note.explanation: A magnet can attract some materials without touching them. Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials; brass, copper, wood, glass and plastic are non-magnetic materials. To tell whether an object is itself a magnet or only a magnetic material, test it with a known magnet: repulsion shows that the object is a magnet.
examples: A paper clip made of iron is attracted to a magnet.
A plastic comb is not attracted to a magnet.
note.checkAnswer: An object that repels a known magnet is a magnet. An object that is only attracted is a magnetic material, not a magnet.
note.simple: A magnet pulls some materials, such as iron, towards it. It does not pull materials such as wood or plastic.
note.checkQuestion: What does repulsion by a known magnet tell you about an object?
note.title: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials
steps: Bring a known magnet close to the object.
If the object repels the magnet, the object is a magnet.
If the object is attracted but does not repel, it is a magnetic material, not a magnet.
note.answer: Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials. Brass, copper, wood, glass and plastic are non-magnetic materials.

examTips: A board question may ask you to define magnetic materials or give examples; learn the section's definition and examples accurately.
For a classification question, sort iron, nickel and cobalt as magnetic, and brass, copper, wood, glass and plastic as non-magnetic.
If asked how magnetic force can be observed without contact, describe the iron-filings activity: the filings follow the magnet moved beneath the sheet.
For a question distinguishing a magnet from a magnetic material, use repulsion with a known magnet as the test; attraction alone is not enough to show that an object is a magnet.

explain.title: Magnetism acts at a distance
explain.body: The textbook defines it this way: “Magnetism is a force that acts at a distance upon magnetic materials.” This means a magnet can attract a magnetic material even when they are not touching.

explain.title: Magnetic materials
explain.body: The textbook says: “These materials are attracted to magnets. These materials are called magnetic materials.” Iron, nickel and cobalt are examples.

explain.title: Non-magnetic materials
explain.body: Brass, copper, wood, glass and plastic are not attracted by the magnet in the section's test. They are called non-magnetic materials.

explain.title: Testing materials
explain.body: Bring a magnet close to an object and observe whether it is attracted. The iron-filings activity also shows magnetic force acting through a card, glass or plastic sheet.

mistakes: Do not say that all metals are magnetic; the section names copper and brass as non-magnetic materials.
Do not confuse a magnetic material with a magnet: a material can be attracted to a magnet without itself being a magnet.
Do not say a magnet must touch an iron object to attract it; the activity shows attraction through a sheet.
When listing examples, do not place glass, wood or plastic among the magnetic materials.
